title: Power Pages: environment-level governance of external authentication providers

reasons: published before the check existed: kept live with a notice while a corrected version is prepared

summary: Hold: the PowerShell command changes who can manage site visibility, not the non-production public-access policy shown beside it. The page also assumes licence inclusion without evidence and says authentication defaults are unclear even though Microsoft documents them.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is in development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development"

claims.claim: Preview is listed for November CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "November CY2026"

claims.claim: General availability is listed for January CY2027.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "January CY2027"

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide, GCC, GCC High and DoD.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)", "GCC", "GCC High", "DoD"]

claims.claim: The release phases are General Availability and Preview.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.claim: The listed platform is Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: Administrators can govern the external authentication options available to Power Pages makers across an environment.
claims.quote: Authentication governance gives you, as an admin, control over which authentication options makers can configure for Power Pages sites in your environments.
claims.fix: Acknowledge that Learn now documents the control while the roadmap remains In development. Flag the authentication-protocol and individual OAuth provider controls as preview, as the cited Learn page does, rather than describing all granular behaviour as final.

claims.claim: Environment-level governance permits site-specific exceptions.
claims.quote: For targeting choices that apply to selected sites, select the sites to include or exclude.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Makers will only see and select approved identity providers.
claims.quote: Makers will only see and select from the approved IDPs when setting up authentication
claims.fix: Distinguish the roadmap wording from current Learn guidance: blocked options remain visible but dimmed and cannot be configured. State that makers can configure only allowed options; cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/security/external-auth-control#what-makers-see.

claims.claim: The roadmap gives Power Platform admin center > Manage > Power Pages > Governance settings > Authentication providers.
claims.quote: Navigate to Manage > Power Pages > Governance settings > Authentication providers.
claims.fix: Keep this explicitly attributed to the roadmap and explain that current Learn uses Manage > Power Pages > Settings > Authentication > option > environment > Manage, as already shown in the table. Identify this as a source difference rather than leaving two unexplained paths.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes configuring allowed or restricted providers, enabling controls for environments and managing site exceptions.
claims.quote: Here, you can configure allowed or restricted external IDPs, enable the control for environments, and manage exceptions for specific sites.

claims.claim: The roadmap entry describes automatic enablement.
claims.quote: Enabled for end users automatically

claims.claim: Whether any restriction applies by default is unclear.
claims.quote: By default, all authentication options are allowed for makers to configure. No action is required unless your organization wants to restrict the options available to makers.
claims.fix: Replace the uncertainty with: 'Learn says all authentication options are allowed by default; administrators configure restrictions if required. Previously configured tenant restrictions are preserved and should be reviewed per environment.' Keep the roadmap's automatic-availability wording separate.

claims.where: What's changing: I found no Learn page yet
claims.claim: There is no Microsoft Learn page describing this feature.
claims.quote: # Use governance controls to manage site authentication
claims.fix: Remove 'I found no Learn page yet.' Cite the already-listed authentication governance page and use its documented defaults, enforcement behaviour and preview qualifications.

claims.claim: The restriction control is admin-opt-in.
claims.quote: By default, all authentication options are allowed for makers to configure. No action is required unless your organization wants to restrict the options available to makers.

claims.claim: Without configured restrictions, makers can choose supported authentication options for a site.
claims.quote: By default, all authentication options are allowed for makers to configure.

claims.claim: Authentication governance is configured in Power Platform admin center > Manage > Power Pages > Settings > Authentication > option > environment > Manage.
claims.quote:
Under **Authentication**, select the authentication option you want to manage.
6. Select an environment, and then select **Manage**.

claims.claim: Authentication options can target all sites, all except selected sites, selected sites only or no sites in an environment.
claims.quote: All sites in this environment | Makers can configure the authentication option for every site in the environment.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an API or automation equivalent for authentication governance.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages authentication governance controls external-auth-control PowerShell API tenant settings; "Power Pages" "authentication" "governance" "API" "PowerShell" external controls. Opened external-auth-control and Set-TenantSettings; no equivalent documented.

claims.claim: Non-production public-access governance is under Manage > Power Pages > Settings > Set site visibility to public access for non-production sites.
claims.quote:
5. Select **Set site visibility to public access for non-production sites**.
6. Select the environment you want to manage.
7. Choose a policy value:
claims.fix: Append '> environment' to controls[1].ui.path and the rendered table so readers reach the policy values.

claims.claim: The non-production public-access policy shown in this row has tenant scope.
claims.quote: Select the environment you want to manage.
claims.fix: Set controls[1].scope to 'environment' and render 'Environment': a tenant administrator selects an environment and can target sites within it. Do not equate the administrator's tenant role with the policy's scope.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table and closing paragraph
claims.claim: Set-TenantSettings with enableSystemAdminsToChangeSiteVisibility = $false is the automation equivalent of the non-production public-access policy.
claims.quote: When you don't want all system administrators to be able to change site visibility, set `enableSystemAdminsToChangeSiteVisibility` to `false`. Then delegate site visibility management to a select set of users.
claims.fix: Remove this command from the non-production public-access row and remove the equivalence asserted below the table. It controls delegation of site-visibility permissions, not the environment's None/All/site-targeting policy. If retained, give it a separate, accurately named tenant delegation row.

claims.where: Governance controls closing paragraph: authentication role
claims.claim: The Power Platform administrator role is required to configure authentication governance.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages authentication governance configure required role Power Platform administrator. Read external-auth-control and admin-roles search excerpts; neither states an exclusive required role for this authentication control.
claims.fix: Remove the assertion that Power Platform administrator is required for authentication governance. State that the feature page describes administrator configuration but does not specify the exact required role.

claims.where: Governance controls closing paragraph: public-access role
claims.claim: The Power Platform administrator role is required to configure the non-production public-access policy.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages authentication governance configure required role Power Platform administrator. Opened site-visibility-governance and site-visibility; the former says tenant admins, while the latter's named roles concern a different site-visibility permissions control.
claims.fix: Replace this part of 'Power Platform admin is required for both settings' with 'Tenant administrators configure non-production public-access governance', matching https://learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/admin/site-visibility-governance. Do not assert an exclusive named role.

claims.where: front matter: licensing; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Feature-specific licensing requirements have not been published, so the licensing model is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages authentication governance external authentication controls licensing Managed Environments license pricing meter. Read external-auth-control, release-plan search excerpt and Power Platform licensing FAQs excerpts; no feature-specific licence requirement stated.

claims.claim: No feature-specific meter is published for this governance control.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages authentication governance external authentication controls licensing Managed Environments license pricing meter. Read external-auth-control and pay-as-you-go meters search excerpt; the latter meters site users, not authentication governance.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Treat it as included in Power Pages
claims.claim: Administrators should treat the authentication governance feature as included in Power Pages.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages authentication governance external authentication controls licensing Managed Environments license pricing meter. Read external-auth-control and Power Platform licensing FAQs excerpts; neither states that this feature is included.
claims.fix: Delete 'Treat it as included in Power Pages.' Retain licensing.model = 'unknown' and say 'Feature-specific licensing and metering have not yet been published; the known preparation cost is administrator time.'

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Managed Environments dependency
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published whether authentication governance depends on Managed Environments.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Pages" "authentication governance" "Managed Environments" license. Read external-auth-control, licensing FAQs and managed-environment-licensing excerpts; no dependency for this authentication control was stated.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: Blocking an authentication option can stop existing users signing in through that option on live sites.
claims.quote: When a governance setting that blocks an authentication option takes effect, users can no longer sign in or register by using that authentication option.

claims.claim: Authentication governance takes precedence over an existing maker configuration that uses a blocked option.
claims.quote: If an existing site configuration uses a sign-in method associated with a blocked option, the governance setting takes precedence.

claims.claim: The prepare action rating fits a low-risk optional restriction control that changes nothing until configured.
claims.quote: No action is required unless your organization wants to restrict the options available to makers.
claims.fix: Set action to 'review'. The standard assigns review to an optional new control with no default behaviour change; the page rates the remaining exposure low, so the high-risk-control exception does not apply.

controlChecks.governs: Which external authentication providers sites in an environment may use

segments: Set site visibility to public access for non-production sites
